newsitem.title: CANADA: Loewen sees strong acquisitions, growth.
newsitem.headline: Loewen sees strong acquisitions, growth.

text.p: Funeral home operator Loewen Group Inc, which defeated a US$2.9 billion hostile takeover bid by rival Service Corp International on Tuesday, expects strong growth in 1997.

Loewen chief financial officer Paul Wagler said in an interview on Wednesday that the company, which has been an aggressive acquirer in the rapidly consolidating funeral industry, agreed with analysts' forecasts that it would do US$600 million to US$700 million in deals this year. "We see that as very reasonable," he said.
Loewen said on Tuesday it had a record US$830 million in acquisitions in 1996, up from US$795 million the prior year.
Loewen's share price fell sharply today after news that Service withdrew its US$45 a share takeover bid, dropping 4-1/4 to a low of 36-5/8 in New York.

Asked if Loewen planned any moves to boost its share price such as a stock buyback program, Wagler said the company currently had no such plans. "I think with 25 percent EPS growth that we achieved in Q3 and everybody is expecting for Q4 and onwards, I think that is about as nice a thank you as anybody could give to your shareholders," he said.

Loewen may consider new issues to raise funds but Wagler declined to discuss details. "We are in the market on a regular basis to raise both debt and equity and I wouldn't exclude raising either of them during the coming months," he said.

As for earnings, Wagler said the company expected profits "to be in line with analysts' expectations." But he declined to comment on specific figures. For the fourth quarter, he said most analysts were expecting earnings per share "in the low 40s (U.S. cents)."
